capabilities.need: Ask the user questions in rounds
capabilities.via: ask_user shows question cards (1 to 4 questions, 2 to 4 options each, one answer per question)
the user picks the project folder with the folder button; bash and the file tools work in it

capabilities.need: Show a file (reel, lab, cards, MP4)
capabilities.via: show_page opens an HTML or video file of the project or the skill in the preview pane

capabilities.need: Fill in the project questions and decide on assets on screens
capabilities.via: the project settings panel (a button in the top bar: audience, message, tone, languages, formats, duration, constraints, control level) and the Resources tab of the Library, in the editing workspace; a new project first asks for its base configuration (conversation and reel languages, formats, target duration and a look), as one question per screen in a wizard (Beginner mode) or as one compact form (Expert mode), and the workspace opens when it is complete (an existing project is never blocked: the checks say what is missing); the guided path ends in the workspace; update_parameter and update_asset change them as plain cards the user accepts or refuses

the project settings panel (Look is a list of six rows, each opening its editor with a back button; while it is open the viewer shows the project's design system as a read-only board, and each editor pins the current choice as a large card above the other options: the looks board, a palette editor with a contrast check, fonts with licence warnings, the default background and its mood, motion moods and the effects pack, each previewed by the same engine as the reel); the catalogues are picked where they are used, with the engine's previews (a background in a scene's Look tab, an animation on an item or in the scene's Effects tab, a scene transition in the transition inspector, the six preview-only transitions shown but never chosen) and an optional floating Catalogue (looks, palettes, backgrounds, effects, transitions) to drag onto a scene, an item or a marker; update_decision changes the global look as plain cards the user accepts or refuses

capabilities.need: Write the storyboard, review each scene and give the go on screens
capabilities.via: the Scenes tab of the Library (the scene library: create, edit, duplicate, archive, rename (a name beside the stable ID, edited in place); every list reorders by dragging a handle, with a gap that opens; each scene opens into a tree of Composition (every element in priority order: words, images and sounds, a linked resource always being one), Effects and Look (background, palette, fonts, each inherited or replaced, with a badge on a scene that replaces something), a click on a group or a node opening the matching inspector tab on that element), the Storyboard strip at the bottom, a film reel (frames sized by duration, each on or off, drag a frame to reorder, drag an edge to stretch, drop a resource, a background, a look, an effect or a transition from the Look and Resources tabs onto a scene, a tree node, an item or a marker (valid targets light up, an invalid drop says why), drop a file from the Finder onto a scene to add and link it, right-click menus, Undo and Redo of every operation (Cmd+Z, Shift+Cmd+Z), transition markers between frames, a playhead, the project's music with its waveform and a snap grid at beat, bar, section or drop, and native reading-budget, feasibility and music checks, which the Checks tab of the left panel groups by area (Project, Resources, Scenes, Storyboard, Music, Build) with a count of what is red or orange, a click opening the element concerned) and the Inspector (tabs Settings, Composition, Effects and Look; Composition is the ordered list of what the scene contains, each element with its words or resource, colour, animation and instruction, each attribute fixed or auto, at a control level of auto, guided or precise; a scene's Look is locked to the project's until a switch per group replaces it for that scene only, and a dropped background, palette or look asks "Replace for this scene only?" first; review: OK, MODIFY or DITCH with a note; the Go button that only the user can press); add_scene, update_scene, enable_scene, move_scene, set_scene_override and add_, update_, remove_ and move_content_item, set_scene_duration, set_transition, set_track and set_grid propose changes as plain cards the user accepts or refuses

capabilities.need: Build the reel, test it and play it
capabilities.via: the Build and preview view of the workspace: after the Go, the app writes vN/film.json (the montage: starts, durations, transitions) and you write the rest of the vN folder (project.json and a main.js in the film format: one module per scene and one SRF.fromData call); the app runs build.py, harness.js and smoke_player.js, shows each result in green or red, and plays vN/dist/index.html in the viewer at the playhead of the reel, with the music; outputs stay in the project folder

capabilities.need: Let the user read and edit the project files next to the assistant
capabilities.via: an Advanced panel (off by default) shows the project's files with editors and a per-file history; propose_edit offers a change to a file as a diff the user accepts or refuses; get_state reads the project's state
screenshot_preview captures the preview pane (a page, a contact sheet or the reel, after show_page) as an image the model can look at

capabilities.fallback: no hosted pages: deliver the HTML file and say how to share it

capabilities.via: bash runs in a login shell in the project folder
numpy and ffmpeg when the owner ran the environment setup; the environment check reports what is missing

capabilities.fallback: no web search: ask the user for facts and documents; never invent figures
